query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid approach combining machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained on ab initio data with enhanced sampling techniques (e.g., metadynamics or nested sampling) can substantially reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties while retaining fidelity to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys or compounds in solid and liquid phases.
generation.intervention: Train machine-learned interatomic potentials (e.g., neural network or Gaussian approximation potentials) on ab initio data and integrate them with enhanced sampling methods to compute free energies and entropy terms for both solid and liquid states.
generation.conditions: Applicable to multicomponent systems with up to 6 elements, at temperatures ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 times the melting temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Machine-learned interatomic potentials capturing vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
generation.mechanism: MLIPs reduce the computational cost of evaluating interatomic interactions while retaining fidelity to ab initio accuracy. Enhanced sampling methods accelerate convergence of free-energy calculations by efficiently exploring phase space, particularly for high-temperature and phase-transition regimes.
generation.predicted_outcome: The hybrid approach will achieve a 10-50x speedup compared to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows, with free-energy and entropy predictions accurate to within 5% of ab initio benchmarks.
generation.baseline: Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD for elemental and binary systems.
generation.boundary: Accuracy and speed gains are expected to diminish for systems with more than 6 components or at temperatures exceeding 1.5 times the melting temperature, where MLIP training data may become insufficient.
generation.uncertainty: The fidelity of MLIPs in capturing complex anharmonic and electron–vibration coupling effects in multicomponent systems is uncertain, as is the efficiency of enhanced sampling methods in high-dimensional composition spaces.

falsification_experiment.design: Benchmark the hybrid approach against explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD for a ternary high-entropy alloy system (e.g., CoCrFe) across a temperature range spanning 0.5 to 1.5 times the melting temperature.
measurements: Free energies of solid and liquid phases
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hybrid approach fails to achieve at least a 10x speedup or deviates by more than 5% from ab initio benchmarks in free-energy or entropy predictions, the hypothesis will be falsified.
